bull_case: Bull value/current price is about 2.23x. Two distinct upside engines exist: custom AI accelerators/networking and infrastructure software/private AI. If AI revenue keeps scaling while software cash conversion holds, the locked Bull path can compound materially above the 9% hurdle.
bear_case: Bear value/current price is only about 0.38x. Customer concentration, roughly 95% TSMC wafer dependence, $126.8B purchase commitments and the AI XPV financing structure can correlate demand, working-capital and residual-value losses in a downturn.
thesis: AVGO has real power-law upside but not a one-sided payoff. Bull/current of 2.23x with at least two value paths supports upside, while Bear/current of 0.38x implies large valuation downside. A 5,000-company growth-persistence base rate now anchors scenario calibration and argues against extrapolating current AI growth, while strong cash generation lowers business-extinction risk.

evidence.claim: Locked DCF values are Bear $137.04, Base $404.48 and Bull $797.84 versus frozen price $357.61; Bull/current is 2.23x and Bear/current is 0.383x.
Q3 FY2026 AI semiconductor revenue was $16.7B, +221% y/y and +54% q/q; Q4 AI semiconductor revenue guidance was $21.7B, +236% y/y.
One semiconductor-solutions distributor represented 50% of Q3 revenue and top five end customers about 55%; about 95% of contract-manufactured wafers were produced by TSMC during 9M FY2026.

At 2026-08-02 Broadcom disclosed $126.821B of unconditional purchase commitments, $3.941B of other contractual commitments and a maximum $29B AI XPV lease backstop; no backstop amounts had been paid and its fair value was not material.
9M FY2026 operating cash flow was $32.950B; the frozen TTM OCF estimate is $40.653B, providing substantial internal funding capacity.
evidence.source: User-supplied 10-Q filed 2026-09-10 plus frozen company_context arithmetic

evidence.claim: McKinsey studied 5,000 of the world's largest public companies over 2005-2019. Only one in eight recorded revenue growth above 10% per year over the decade; only one in three top-growth-quartile firms sustained that rate in the next five years, and the rate was one in four for predominantly organic growers.

counterevidence: The Bull path requires a company already above $1.7T market cap to exceed $3T-equivalent value; scale itself limits plausible multiple expansion.
The $179.2B RPO is not a clean backlog proxy: the filing explicitly says RPO is not indicative of revenue for future periods.
AI XPV improves demand financing but also couples Broadcom to customer lease economics through a potential $29B backstop.
A 50% distributor revenue share and 55% top-five end-customer share make supposedly independent AI upside paths less independent than segment labels imply.
unknowns: No pre-cutoff empirical base-rate dataset was found that isolates Broadcom-like megacap custom-AI semiconductor companies; the McKinsey base rate is deliberately broad.
Economic terms and customer identities behind the largest custom-AI contracts remain undisclosed.
The probability and funding mechanics of up to $42B of conditional customer convertible notes are not quantified.
How much of the $179.2B RPO is cancellable, low-margin or tied to AI XPV-supported deployments is not separately disclosed.
falsifiers: Bull asymmetry weakens materially if AI semiconductor growth falls below 30% while software growth also falls below 10% for two consecutive quarters.
Permanent-loss resilience weakens if backstop exposure becomes funded while TTM OCF falls below $25B or net debt exceeds 2x TTM OCF.
The concentration bear case weakens if top-five end-customer share falls below 40% without sacrificing AI growth.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 현재가격이 비현실적인 Bull Case 이상을 요구
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Frozen price $357.61 is far below locked Bull value $797.84; the veto's sole element is not met.

hard_veto_flags.veto: 파산 또는 영구손실 확률이 기대수익에 비해 지나치게 높음
hard_veto_flags.rationale: Bear valuation still assumes positive owner FCF and meaningful going-concern value, while current OCF and liquidity are substantial. The large Bear price drawdown is valuation risk, not evidence of business-value extinction; AI XPV commitments remain a scored tail risk.

key_kpis.name: AI XPV funded exposure + backstop utilization
key_kpis.threshold: no material funded loss; review if >$10B funded exposure

next_checks: Quantify the customer and contract split of AI RPO and XPV-supported deployments.
Replace the broad large-company base rate if a pre-cutoff semiconductor/custom-AI-specific persistence dataset becomes available.
Recompute Bear/current and Bull/current after FY2027 guidance and any backstop funding.

subscores.rationale: Bull/current is 2.23x, inside the 1.6-2.5 observable band, and at least two distinct paths are visible: AI silicon/networking and infrastructure software. The 90 row is excluded because the ratio is below 2.5x and the company is already megacap.

Bear/current is 0.383. Band-centre interpolation within the 0.2-0.4 row produces about 56 and rounds to 55 on the 5-point grid. No +10 modifier applies because AVGO is net debt, while no -15 applies because 12-month survival does not require external capital.

The rerun now uses an empirical base rate: McKinsey's 5,000-largest-public-company study found only 1/8 sustained >10% annual revenue growth over a decade and only 1/3 of top-quartile growers sustained their rate into the next five years. Combined with explicit Bear/Base/Bull sensitivity, this meets the 75 'base rate/sensitivity used' anchor. 90 is excluded because the base rate is broad rather than custom-AI/semiconductor-specific.

uncertainties.rationale: AI silicon and networking are economically linked to the same hyperscaler/frontier-lab capex cycle, reducing path independence.
The $29B backstop and very large purchase commitments create correlated downside if AI customers fail to absorb contracted capacity.
The new base rate is empirical but broad. It improves calibration discipline without establishing a precise AVGO-specific scenario probability.
